content.comment_body: Is there any encoder that works with the [product_name] high-speed input I3?
[product_name] isn't the most suitable controller for encoder integration.
Thanks, do you know the reason for this?

While pulse counting happens independently of the processing cycle, the actual evaluation is restricted to the cycle itself. Depending on the encoder type, this can cause inaccuracies when checking limits. Similarly, if using A/B encoders, querying the direction may lead to errors, as direction determination also happens within the cycle.

It is manageable to use an encoder with few pulses per revolution and at a slow rotation speed, assuming the application doesn't demand high accuracy. For example, a setup in a referenced project uses a 100 pulse per revolution encoder running at around 17 RPM.

analysis.insight_summary: Users address the compatibility of encoders with [product_name] modules, highlighting limitations in how pulses and directions are evaluated only during processor cycles. Concerns center on the risk of inaccuracies at higher speeds or with complex encoders. Nonetheless, one user mentions that simple, low-speed encoders can still be used for basic tasks where precision isn't critical.
analysis.user_expectations: Expectations are that [product_name] should reliably interface with encoders, enabling accurate pulse counting and direction sensing, even when operating at moderate speeds.
